turns: Which LGAs had the largest share of land flooded in 2024?
reply:
*Flooding: Sokoto State* — experimental

Across the 23 LGAs of Sokoto State, the 2024 share of land under floodwater (radar) ranged from 0.0% (Sokoto South) to 8.5% (Sokoto North); the median was 0.6%. Most land under water: Sokoto North (8.5%), Kebbe (2.4%), Tambuwal (2.2%). Least: Sokoto South (0.0%), Dange Shuni (0.1%), Isa (0.2%).

In 2024, radar saw 26,000 ha of Sokoto State under water at some point (18,590 ha on farmland, 4,880 ha in the river floodplain, 2,540 ha on other land). Satellite radar saw floodwater in Sokoto State in every rainy season 2015–2026; the largest was 2020, with 58,430 ha under water at some point (41,290 ha on farmland, 10,320 ha in the river floodplain, 6,820 ha on other land). In 2026, radar saw 4,020 ha of Sokoto State under water at some point (2,690 ha on farmland, 630 ha in the river floodplain, 700 ha on other land). UNOSAT's event map of 5–9 September 2024 and 9–13 November 2024, built over several days, shows 123,410 ha and catches more of the flood than single radar passes. Radar can't judge 35% of Sokoto State (built-up land, dense trees, dry sand); there, flood reports are the source.

Sources: Copernicus GFM radar, UNOSAT, JRC; details in show working. Information only, not an official flood warning.
